rationale: Methods, Intervention: "a researcher-developed 3D health video game adapted from Escape from Diab"; played at home on CD (Inclusion criteria: "access to a computer or laptop"); no movement-as-input described, only goal-setting, feedback and mini-games in a narrative game.
doubt: I1: the paper calls it a health/serious video game and cites active video games; if a seated PC game with no movement input is borderline for I1 is left to the criterion's 'seated video game' exclusion.

rationale: I5 instrument: BREQ-2 (Measurements: "The BREQ-2 has 19 items assessing the continuum of behavioral regulation in exercise"). I6 results for both arms: Results, Table 2 gives baseline and 4-week means for Intervention and Control per subscale; "The significant time×group interactions were observed on identified regulation". VR cycling exergames (Le Tour, Race Car) for 4 weeks vs no-intervention control; randomized by computer-generated sequence; published 2025-12-15.

I5 instrument: MSPPA (Outcome measures: "The MSPPA is a validated 16-item, 5-point Likert-type scale scored from 16 to 80 that measures motivation to participate in physical activity"). I6: Results, Table 4 gives T0/T1/T2 for CG and RGBEG and "a significantly smaller decline in motivation in the RGBEG than in the CG". 24-week programme; random allocation; control gets conventional exercise; published 2026.
doubt: I1: balance-board and camera pose-based games (BeCure Balance, Smart Pose Runner) are described only briefly in the main text, game mechanics are in Appendix 2 and not seen; whether limb or trunk movement is the game input and a goal or score is pursued is not fully settled. I1: the game arm is a mixed programme and the first 4 weeks were conventional in both arms.

rationale: Abstract: "The key themes from the interviews indicated that the KneeBRIGHT games are motivating"; outcomes were KOOS, IKDC, strength and balance, TAM and SUS only in the game arm, and motivation appears only in interviews.
doubt: I1: EMG-biofeedback game controlled by quadriceps contraction (with weight shifting, mini-squats); whether muscle activation counts as limb or trunk movement as game input is unclear, so E1 might also apply.

rationale: Methods, Study and Trial Designs: participants were initially randomly allocated but "requested to change their assigned allocation, and these requests were accommodated to minimize participant dropout"; analysis was per protocol by group actually joined; the paper calls itself quasi-experimental.
doubt: I2: allocation was random but 9-10% of participants per group switched by preference before the start; the criterion does not say how much departure from random allocation still counts as randomized.
